D.t: Everett Wess trails by 17.0 and wins 1% of simulations. Closing it takes about 146,023 voters switching sides, or 292,047 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +25.2 and R +8.9. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +14.5. Your best recent poll is Chism Strategies (D) at R +9.4; your worst is The Alabama Poll at R +21.2. 4 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Jefferson, a projected net 74,129 votes; Montgomery, a projected net 34,723 votes; Madison, a projected net 10,129 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Madison, D +7.0, 8.5% of the vote; Mobile, R +0.8, 7.8% of the vote; Tuscaloosa, R +1.1, 3.9% of the vote; Chambers, R +10.7, 0.6% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Everett Wess runs furthest behind in Cullman, Blount, Walker. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters without a degree, 67% of voters, 40 to 59, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.37 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 63% of voters, 40 to 59, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.17 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 45 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.96 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Everett Wess: Immigration voters 13 to 86, White voters 30 to 69, Incomes $125K and up 33 to 66. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$18K cash against $627K. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points away from Everett Wess. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $16.8M helping Barry Moore and $0 helping Everett Wess.

R.t: Barry Moore leads by 17.0 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 292,047 votes; a one point swing is about 8,580 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +8.9 and R +25.2. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +14.5. Your best recent poll is The Alabama Poll at R +21.2; your worst is Chism Strategies (D) at R +9.4. 4 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Baldwin, a projected net 47,887 votes; Shelby, a projected net 24,976 votes; Cullman, a projected net 24,578 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Madison, D +7.0, 8.5% of the vote; Mobile, R +0.8, 7.8% of the vote; Tuscaloosa, R +1.1, 3.9% of the vote; Chambers, R +10.7, 0.6% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Barry Moore runs furthest behind in Jefferson, Tuscaloosa, Talladega. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters without a degree, 67% of voters, 59 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.37 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 63% of voters, 59 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.17 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 54 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.96 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Barry Moore: Black voters 20 to 79, Independents 24 to 74, Moderates 39 to 60. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$627K cash against $18K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points toward Barry Moore. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
